title: Key Word Transformation: Inversion and Emphasis (Set 2)
instructions: For questions 1-6, complete the second sentence so that it has a similar meaning to the first sentence, using the word given. Do not change the word given. You must use between three and six words, including the word given.

items.sentence1: I didn't understand how serious the situation was until I read the full report.
items.sentence2Suffix: I read the full report did I understand how serious the situation was.
items.explanation: 'Only when + clause + inverted auxiliary (did/was/had)' is an emphatic structure meaning something became true only at that specific point.

items.sentence1: I have never felt so embarrassed in my entire life.
items.sentence2Suffix: I felt so embarrassed in my entire life.
items.explanation: 'Never + auxiliary + subject' is an inverted structure used for emphasis, equivalent to 'I have never felt...' but more dramatic.

items.sentence1: She is both an excellent violinist and a gifted composer.
items.sentence2Suffix: an excellent violinist but also a gifted composer.
items.explanation: 'Not only + inverted auxiliary + subject...but also' is a fixed emphatic structure linking two qualities, requiring subject-verb inversion after 'not only'.

items.sentence1: I have hardly ever seen such a dramatic improvement in such a short time.
items.sentence2Suffix: I seen such a dramatic improvement in such a short time.
items.explanation: 'Rarely + auxiliary + subject' is an inverted structure with a similar meaning to 'hardly ever', used for emphasis at the start of a sentence.

items.sentence1: The team most urgently needed more funding, not more staff.
items.sentence2Suffix: the team most urgently needed was more funding, not more staff.
items.explanation: A 'what' cleft sentence ('What + clause + be + focus') is used to emphasise a particular element of the sentence — here, the thing that was needed.

items.sentence1: The design flaw, not the weather, ultimately caused the bridge's collapse.
items.sentence2Suffix: the design flaw, not the weather, that ultimately caused the bridge's collapse.
items.explanation: An 'it' cleft sentence ('It + be + focus + that...') is used to emphasise which specific element was responsible for the result.
